quick: With food to reduce GI upset
summary: Sodium valproate is a broad-spectrum antiepileptic and mood stabilizer effective in generalized and partial seizures, absence seizures, bipolar mania and migraine prophylaxis. Dosing is weight-based (10-15 mg/kg/day initial, up to 60 mg/kg/day). Boxed warnings cover fatal hepatotoxicity (highest in children <2), major teratogenicity (neural tube defects, reduced IQ) and pancreatitis. Contraindicated in hepatic disease, urea-cycle and POLG mitochondrial disorders.
indications: Simple and complex absence seizures (sole and adjunctive)
Multiple seizure types including absence seizures (adjunctive)
Acute manic or mixed episodes of bipolar disorder

dosage.d: Initial 10-15 mg/kg/day; increase by 5-10 mg/kg/day weekly
Initial 750 mg/day (or 25 mg/kg with ER); titrate to effect
ER 500 mg once daily for 1 week then 1000 mg/day
Same total daily dose as oral, infused over 60 min (<=20 mg/min)
dosage.n: Switch to oral as soon as feasible; not studied beyond 14 days

admin: Swallow enteric-coated/ER tablets whole; do not crush or chew
Take with food to reduce gastrointestinal irritation
Sprinkle capsules may be opened onto soft food and swallowed without chewing
Perform liver function tests before therapy and at frequent intervals, especially in first 6 months
Do not stop abruptly in epilepsy - risk of status epilepticus; taper gradually
moa: Valproate increases brain concentrations of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), likely by enhancing synthesis and reducing degradation, and blocks voltage-gated sodium channels and T-type calcium channels. These actions reduce high-frequency neuronal firing and stabilize neuronal membranes.

absolute: Hepatic disease or significant hepatic dysfunction
Known mitochondrial disorders due to POLG mutations (e.g. Alpers-Huttenlocher); suspected POLG disorder in children <2 yr
Pregnancy/women of childbearing potential without effective contraception for migraine prophylaxis
relative: Women of childbearing potential (use only if alternatives fail)
monitor: Serum ammonia if lethargy/mental status change

preg: High teratogenic potential - causes neural tube defects, other major malformations, decreased IQ and neurodevelopmental disorders. Contraindicated in pregnancy for migraine and should not be used in women of childbearing potential for epilepsy or bipolar disorder unless other treatments fail. Effective contraception is essential; supplement folic acid before/during pregnancy if used.
lact: Valproate is excreted in breast milk in low concentrations and breastfeeding is generally considered compatible. Monitor the infant for jaundice, drowsiness and unusual bruising/bleeding.
renal: Use with caution; reduced protein binding in renal impairment increases free drug fraction - interpret total levels cautiously and consider monitoring free valproate.
hepatic: Contraindicated in hepatic disease or significant hepatic dysfunction. Fatal hepatotoxicity occurs mainly in the first 6 months and is highest in children under 2 and patients with mitochondrial disorders.

major: Lamotrigine - valproate raises lamotrigine levels and serious rash risk; reduce lamotrigine dose
Carbapenems (meropenem, etc.) - markedly reduce valproate levels and seizure control; avoid
Topiramate - increased risk of hyperammonemia/encephalopathy and hypothermia
moderate: Phenytoin, phenobarbital, carbamazepine - complex bidirectional level changes
Aspirin - displaces valproate, raising free levels
interactions.food: Take with food; food slightly delays but does not reduce absorption.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol - additive CNS depression and hepatic strain.
interactions.diagnostics: May raise liver enzymes and ammonia, lower platelets, and cause false-positive urine ketone tests.

emergency: Acute hepatic failure (malaise, anorexia, vomiting, jaundice)

monitoring: Liver function tests at baseline and frequently in first 6 months
Complete blood count and platelets/coagulation before surgery and periodically
Serum valproate level (therapeutic 50-100 mcg/mL; up to 125 for mania)
Ammonia level if unexplained lethargy, vomiting or mental status change
Pregnancy status and contraception in women of childbearing potential
counsel: Do not stop suddenly - this can trigger seizures
Report yellowing of skin/eyes, severe abdominal pain, vomiting or unusual bruising/bleeding
Women: use reliable contraception and discuss risks before pregnancy due to birth defects
Avoid alcohol and report excessive drowsiness or confusion
Swallow extended-release tablets whole and take with food
pk: Anticonvulsant effect within days; steady state in 2-4 days
pearls: Boxed warnings: fatal hepatotoxicity, teratogenicity (neural tube defects/low IQ), pancreatitis
Highest hepatotoxicity risk in children <2 and patients with mitochondrial disease
Carbapenems can dramatically drop valproate levels - avoid the combination
Check ammonia for unexplained encephalopathy even with normal liver enzymes
Avoid in women of childbearing potential unless no alternative; the IV form is only a temporary substitute for oral
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is nearly time for the next dose, skip the missed one and continue the schedule. Do not double up. Missing doses in epilepsy can precipitate seizures.
overdose: Overdose may cause somnolence, heart block, deep coma, hyperammonemia and respiratory depression; very high levels can be fatal. Provide supportive care, naloxone may partially reverse CNS depression, and hemodialysis or carnitine supplementation can be used for severe toxicity. Monitor for cerebral edema.
